other.process description: two-step melting: first melt non-reactive metals (Ni, Fe, Mo) with controlled carbon-boil to remove nitrogen, then add Cr and Nb master alloys, Ti, Al, B

evidence.quote: This is done by a two-step melting process. In the first one the nitrogen is taken out a bath formed with the non-reactive metals (Ni, Fe, Mo) by a controlled carbon-boil. Subsequently Cr and Nb bearing master alloys with extra-low nitrogen content (produced by a special smelting process developed by the company) are added to the bath, together with Ti, Al and B.

evidence.quote: following the last ESR step, small Al-oxides were observed in the microstructure of both ingots, Fig. 5. The Al-oxide inclusions were characterized using EDS as Al2O3 with trace amounts of Mg and Ca detected within.

mechanisms.name: Al pick-up by Ti reduction of alumina from slag

evidence.quote: During ESR, reactive elements such as Ti have been reported to reduce the alumina and may lead to Al pick-up following the reaction of Eq. 2 [20, 21]: 3 Ti½C metal +2 Al2O3ðÞ slag → 3 TiO2ðÞ slag +4 Al½C metal ð2Þ
This is attributed to the removal of inclusions by the slag. Inclusions such as TiN potentially form during VIM are most likely dissolved in the molten slag [17, 18].
